artifacts.summary: Locates the HEAD-binding at exactly two call sites (please-grant.sh mint, pg_grant_find_match consume), proposes a single action_class=push_branch-gated refs/heads/${REF} resolution that subsumes the checked-out-branch case for free, confirms guard-git-push.sh and git-push-granted.sh need no change, and confirms no context doc needs a correction.

memory_candidates.content: In a consent-gated push-grant mechanism (mint hook writes a KV grant file with HMAC; a PreToolUse guard matches and consumes it), a 'bind to HEAD' defect for a non-checked-out ref is fixable at exactly the two symmetric call sites (mint-time write, consume-time match) with a single substitution gated on the action class that can ever name a non-checked-out ref -- resolving refs/heads/<name> instead of HEAD. Because a checked-out branch's refs/heads/<name> always equals HEAD by git's own definition, this one substitution reproduces the old behavior for the checked-out case automatically, with no separate 'is this the checked-out branch' conditional needed.

When a dispatch's territory lists several files for a bugfix (e.g. a hook, a guard, a wrapper, a lib), a call-site survey (grep for every caller of the function being fixed) can establish that some listed files are test-coverage spectators needing zero code change, not oversights -- worth doing explicitly before planning edits to every listed file.
